newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bill market subdued by peso volatility.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bill market subdued by peso volatility.

text.p: The Philippine secondary market for Treasury bills was kept quiet by the volatility in the peso, traders said on Monday.
The peso hit a record low of 30.11 in Monday's morning deals. Its previous low was 30 last month after it had a de facto devaluation.
"Banks are still cautious. We wouldn't be surprised if the central bank raised liquidity reserves again," a foreign bank dealer said.
Last week, the central bank raised liquidity reserves to five percent from four percent to keep a check on funds that might be used for peso speculation.
Higher reserves could result in a tightening of liquidity which would raise interest rates again and make it expensive to hold on to lower interest yielding T-bills, traders said.
The average interbank call loan rate rose to 14.15625 percent from 14.0625 percent due to the effect of the additional liquidity reserves, dealers said.
Volume was higher at 18.27 billion pesos from 8.12 billion.
The market had 39 lenders and 21 borrowers.
